synopsis: ASME guidance distinguishes verification of implementation against mathematics, validation against the real application, and uncertainty quantification; these activities assess model credibility relative to its context of use [f14531, f10601, f9748]. Calibration against a test does not establish predictive capability on independent data, and the booklet cites ASME alongside NASA as requiring real-world validation rather than internal consistency alone [f8159, f14535, f14952]. The cited portfolio includes V&V 40-2018, V&V 10 (2019), and VVUQ 30.1-2024, with the latter addressing scaling methodologies, applicability justification, and uncertainty treatment [f9748, f7664]. The planning chapter synthesizes ASME and other frameworks into a proposed safety-claim decomposition, while the review chapter recommends a one-page credibility map for all seven reviewers [f9725, f10908]. The booklet emphasizes credibility and uncertainty over simulation counts and infers that, without an auditable evidence chain for one slice before prototype arrival, more scenarios add questionable evidence rather than assurance [f10884, f10796]. Even if virtual testing cannot replace most final physical evidence by mid-2027, the booklet identifies a useful hybrid role in defect discovery, scenario exploration, and selecting informative physical tests [f10987].
